stories.title: How will data centers impact Michigan’s renewable energy goals? It’s complicated, new research says
stories.summary: New research indicates that Michigan's data center growth, including facilities in Saline and Van Buren Townships, complicates the state's 2035 renewable energy goals. While data centers may fund new renewable generation and storage, their substantial energy demand could necessitate increased reliance on natural gas and challenge utilities' ability to meet targets without delays, requiring significant land for solar expansion.

stories.title: Work stops on Google data center project after Wayne County says it lacks permit
stories.summary: Wayne County has issued a stop-work order for Google's "Project Cannoli" data center in Van Buren Township, citing a lack of proper county construction permits and potential impacts on county drains. The developer, Panattoni, is accused of working within easement areas and obstructing drains, creating flood risks. The project is expected to require significant power, equivalent to a city's electricity needs.

stories.summary: The University of Michigan's School of Education now offers a direct admission program for freshmen, allowing students to begin education coursework immediately. This aims to better prepare future teachers and address nationwide shortages by providing earlier engagement with the profession and more practice in supported environments.

stories.title: New net-zero community will become Michigan’s first virtual power plant
stories.summary: Ann Arbor's Veridian at County Farm, a net-zero energy community, is launching Michigan's first residential virtual power plant pilot. DTE Energy will remotely control residents' home batteries to inject stored solar power into the grid during peak demand, potentially reducing utility costs and strengthening reliability for consumers. The pilot aims to test this approach for future scalability.

photo.alt: Powerful living: The net-zero energy community Veridian at County Farm will host Michigan’s first residential virtual power plant with battery manufacturer Sonnen USA.

stories.title: AAPS officials say new teacher contract is a step forward, but not a final fix
stories.summary: Ann Arbor Public Schools and the Ann Arbor Education Association reached a contract agreement in September, including a 1.5% salary raise for some staff and a 5% increase in the district's healthcare budget. Officials view it as a step toward financial recovery, but not a final fix for teacher concerns.

stories.title: A look back: Gretchen Whitmer 8 years as Michigan’s governor
stories.summary: As Governor Whitmer concludes her eight-year term, her administration's impact includes repairing over 20,000 lane miles and 1,400 bridges, approving nearly $2 billion annually for roads, and expanding childcare subsidies to make 105,000 more children eligible. Free K-12 school meals were also implemented statewide, though some programs face vulnerability as federal pandemic-era funds diminish.

inputFacts.title: Are you registered to vote in Michigan? Here's how to check ahead of November general election
inputFacts.summary: The 2026 November general election sample ballot can be viewed through the Michigan Voter Information Center. Voters may cast split tickets or choose straight-ticket options for partisan races, though straight-ticket selections do not automatically include non-partisan races.

inputFacts.title: Rewriting Michigan’s constitution?: Understanding Proposal 1 on the November 2026 ballot
inputFacts.summary: Proposal 1 on Michigan's 2026 November ballot asks voters whether to convene a constitutional convention in 2027 to draft a general revision of the state constitution for voter approval or rejection. The proposal will appear as 'Proposal 2026-1: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution' on the ballot.

inputFacts.title: Humane Society of Huron Valley offers pet safety tips for holiday season
inputFacts.summary: The Humane Society of Huron Valley is providing advice to pet owners to ensure animal safety during the busy holiday season. Recommendations include creating quiet spaces for anxious pets, planning ahead for boarding, and keeping dangerous foods like those containing xylitol away from animals.

inputFacts.title: Holidays not so happy? Mental health help is available
inputFacts.summary: As the holiday season approaches, many individuals experience increased stress, grief, and loneliness due to personal and professional demands. The Washtenaw County Health Department encourages those feeling overwhelmed to seek support through local resources like the 'Wish You Knew' campaign or by calling 988.

inputFacts.title: Democrat victory in special election may show where 2026 midterms are headed
inputFacts.summary: Democrat Chedrick Greene won a special election for Michigan's 35th state Senate district seat by a large margin, a district that previously supported President Trump in 2024. The race highlighted differing campaign strategies, with Greene focusing on national affordability issues and Republican Jason Tunney emphasizing local concerns. The outcome may signal broader trends for the 2026 midterm elections.

inputFacts.title: Starlings and Ghost Light usher in a new era for Hamtramck’s music scene
inputFacts.summary: The band Starlings, composed of former Handgrenades members, is set to perform at Ghost Light to celebrate the venue's 10th anniversary. The event will also mark the official unveiling of the venue's newly expanded performance space.

inputFacts.title: Detroit’s America’s Thanksgiving Parade celebrates 100 years on Woodward Avenue
inputFacts.summary: Detroit’s America’s Thanksgiving Parade marks its 100th anniversary on November 26, 2026, featuring 33 floats and a performance by the Detroit Youth Choir. The event, led by grand marshal Dan Gilbert, begins at 8:45 a.m. on Woodward Avenue.
